I have a 1TB internal SSD I use for media storage. It's not my boot volume. I have more RAM than I know what do with, and my pagefile is on a different drive. Currently this drive has ~60GB free and rarely receives any writes. Is there a negative performance impact if I fill this drive up? If so, how large of an impact can I expect, and what percentage needs to be kept free?
Does filling a SSD negatively impact performance?

Yes filling a SSD brings down performance but also lowers the life expectancy. (Depending on the used technology)

But lower performance also happens on hard disks when they gets filled. The head has to get further and further and I think if halves the read/write speeds compared to an near empty disk.

Would you expect lower SSD life expectancy to still be the case if the content is 99% static? Filling drives usually goes hand-in-hand with with frequent writes, which will burn through SSDs. In this case it's basically a static drive (it's mostly a movie collection, so what's there isn't going to change/move/etc).

I'm pretty familiar with the performance/lifespan hit for HDDs, but SSDs not so much.

It depends on the used technology I believe. modern SSD's are better than the ones a few years ago.

http://www.digitaltrends.com/computing/the-care-and-feeding-of-solid-state-drives/

if your OS is on it, having it full could cause problems when the system try to updates the various logs it use and fragmentation coud lead to slower loadings ( but given SSD already play musical chairs with data internally ( wear leveling ), I doubt it would have much of an effect ).

if not, no way.
My OS is on a seperate drive. This is just a static file storage drive for my movies and music. There should be minimal change on it, which is why I'm not certain if conventional wisdom applies.

If it's purely storage, it won't impact your system at all, and for the drive itself, the slowdown will only happen for a few files at worst ( due to some fragmentation ) and even then the speed of SSDs would make it virtually unnoticeable ( unless you need to play all your files at once ).
Beside, what's the point of storage if you can't use it?
